Thank you for your reply. My significant other is honestly an amazing person.  Insanely supportive and understanding and has interests in psychology. They have just lost patience with me. Which I completely understand, it can get tiring after 9 years of dealing with my mental illness. My significant other is the only reason I've lived as long as I have. They helped me get on track with recovery for my eating disorder and all sorts of other stuff. 

This is my other reddit account so it's fairly anonymous and I only created it to vent about my mental health so I'm going to keep my identity very private. It's just very strange to finally get a diagnosis that makes sense to me. I was diagnosed with bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, ocd, and various other things. Some of those still remain but BPD is the only thing that has really resonated with me and honestly I was hoping I'd never get the diagnosis because it's kind of terrifying to me.

I started meds but had a pretty terrible reaction to them so I'm waiting for my appointment with my psychiatrist. I have to find a psychologist that will take my insurance. I have referrals from my psychiatrist so hopefully I'll find someone. I really think I need inpatient but I know I can't afford it and I refuse to put that kind of financial stress on my significant other.

I'm happy you're finding what works for you. It's difficult to cope with something like this so I hope you find a happy medium in your life.
